segments.expected: One. The cord came off the elbow and across the neck, and Pru's left thumb came down on it, flat, and pinned it.
segments.transcript: One. The cord came off the elbow and across the neck, and Prue's left thumb came down on it, flat, and pinned it.

segments.expected: Two. The right hand took the long end over and under. The thumb stayed where it was.
segments.transcript: Two. The right hand took the long end over and under. The thumb stayed where it was.

segments.expected: "Saturday the 22nd. The Low Lane. A rung to a bag under a porch; seventeen thrown, twelve sealed. Lit: Pryce, a porch, 0.16. Renn, two cuts on the post, 0.07. Talley, three, 0.09. segments.transcript: Saturday the 22nd. The low lane. A rung to a bag under a porch. 17 thrown, 12 sealed. Lit. Price. A porch. 0.16. Ren. Two cuts on the post. 0.07. Tally. 3. 0.09. Rowan. Nothing. Dark on her healer's card. Cade. Nothing. A clock. He did not smile. Spent. 0.32. Held. 25.21. Sealed. Medical. 0.8.

segments.expected: He had never been let write anything down, because Orla had had it all worked out for him beforehand; she had built him a step at a time, with every step explained, and she had been proud of how little there was left for him to find.
segments.transcript: He had never been let write anything down, because Orla had had it all worked out for him beforehand. She had built him a step at a time, with every step explained. And she had been proud of how little there was left for him to find.

segments.expected: So she wanted it, and it would feel like paying something; and that was the best reason in the world to keep her hands off it. A sponsor who used one candidate to settle her account with another had learned nothing whatever.
segments.transcript: So she wanted it, and it would feel like paying something, and that was the best reason in the world to keep her hands off it. A sponsor who used one candidate to settle her account with another had learned nothing whatever.

segments.expected: "There's always a rest. I'm not asking what it is. I only know that when somebody says the method, there's a pile on the other side of the table." Orla's voice was rough. "I kept a pile from him. He knows it."
segments.transcript: There's always a rest, I'm not asking what it is. I only know that when somebody says the method, there's a pile on the other side of the table. Orla's voice was rough. I kept a pile from him, he knows it.

segments.expected: There was a pile. Her sponsor did not know what was in it, and was not to. It was no part of any yard.
segments.transcript: It was a pile. Her sponsor did not know what was in it and was not to. It was no part of any yard.

segments.expected: It was. The Hunt: a licensed hunt on tidal ground, under company officers. Marked on clean yield after shares, less every remark. A four holding a Flask license in its own right hunts on its own entry. A four without one hunts attached. Students close nothing.
segments.transcript: It was. The hunt. A licensed hunt on tidal ground, under company offices, marked on clean yield after shares, less every remark. A four, holding a flask license in its own right, hunts on its own entry. A four without one, hunts attached. Students close nothing.

segments.expected: "Sixty," said Perrin. "Sixty-one. I'm told that I'm to go on."
segments.transcript: Sixty, said Perrin, sixty-one. I'm told that I'm to go on.

segments.expected: The second was plainer. She wanted him to have the book.
segments.transcript: The second was Plena. She wanted him to have the book.

segments.expected: She wanted it more than she had wanted anything since she came off the Line. She wanted a man of forty on the south coast to sit down with those pages and see what a seventeen-year-old with his kind of trouble had done when it went wrong. The girl had written it down: I stacked, and I can't weigh it, and the count is somebody else's, in pencil, with the cost beside it, and she had not torn out a leaf.
segments.transcript: She wanted it more than she had wanted anything since she came off the line. She wanted a man of forty on the south coast to sit down with those pages and see what a seventeen-year-old with his kind of trouble had done when it went wrong. The girl had written it down, I stacked and I can't weigh it and the count is somebody else's, in pencil with the cost beside it, and she had not torn out a leaf.

segments.expected: She had got that far by the Wednesday, and had been rather comfortable there.
segments.transcript: She had got that far by the Wednesday and had been rather comfortable there.

segments.expected: "If I leave a thing out," she said, "I'll say that I've left one out. I'll not say what it is. He'll know that there's a gap, and that I put it there on purpose."
segments.transcript: If I leave a thing out, she said, I'll say that I've left one out. I'll not say what it is. He'll know that there's a gap and that I put it there on purpose.
